statement: Show that $x^{4}+4$ factorises as $(x^{2}+2x+2)(x^{2}-2x+2)$, and hence find the four complex roots of the equation $x^{4}+4=0$.
solution: Using the difference of two squares, $(x^{2}+2)^{2}-(2x)^{2}=(x^{2}+2x+2)(x^{2}-2x+2)=x^{4}+4$. Setting this to zero gives $x^{2}+2x+2=0$ or $x^{2}-2x+2=0$, whose roots are $x=-1\pm i$ and $x=1\pm i$ respectively.
